best_for: People moving off Evernote or a similar app who want end-to-end encrypted notes on every device, and who mostly write text so the free plan's attachment limits won't bite.
description:
Notesnook is a note-taking app from Streetwriters, made for the notes you would not want anyone else to read, such as medical results or bank details. Its homepage says Privacy Guides recommends it.

The editor handles tables, checklists, code blocks, math formulas, outlines and Markdown. You can lock the app with a fingerprint, PIN or password, and put your most private notes in a vault with a second password. Links between notes work both ways, so each note shows what points back to it. You can publish a single note as a web page, with a password if you like, and clip web articles without the ads. An Inbox API lets Zapier, IFTTT or your own script drop notes into your account.

points.title: Free covers text, not big files
points.text: The free plan gives unlimited notes on unlimited devices, but only 50 MB of attachment uploads a month, 10 MB per file, 50 notebooks, 50 tags, 10 active reminders and 100 versions per note.

points.title: Paid plans buy storage
points.text: Essential is USD 1.99 a month or 19.99 a year (1 GB a month, 100 MB files, 500 notebooks). Pro is 6.99 a month or 69.99 a year (10 GB, 1 GB files, no notebook cap). Believer is 8.99 a month or 89.99 a year (25 GB, 5 GB files). Essential and Pro have a 14-day trial. Prices include tax and were read on the date below.

points.title: Open source down to the server
points.text: The desktop, web and mobile apps and the sync server are all published under GPLv3. Notes are encrypted on your device before they sync, so the server only stores unreadable data.

points.title: Keep your recovery key
points.text: If you forget your password, what you get back depends on your data recovery key or a backup file. With neither, the only way back in wipes every note, notebook and attachment, and Notesnook cannot restore them.

points.title: Bring your old notes
points.text: The importer in the desktop and web apps reads exports from Evernote, Google Keep, Joplin, Obsidian, Simplenote and others, plus Markdown, HTML and plain text. Imports run on your device.

points.title: Linux: verified Flatpak, one step behind
points.text: The Flathub build is marked verified as published by Streetwriters, for x64 and Arm64. It sits at v3.4.12 while Windows and macOS are at 3.4.13. On Windows the installer is per-user, with portable builds, for x64 and Arm64. Macs get separate Intel and Apple silicon .dmg files.

points.title: Older versions on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 87 versions. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
